failures.title: Aston Martin AJ133S Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: Timing Chain Tensioner Wear
items.whatHappens: Early iterations of the AJ133 family (pre-2013) were prone to timing chain tensioner wear, which could lead to chain slack and a distinct rattling noise on cold starts. While the Vantage S (introduced in 2012) benefited from some revisions, high-mileage units or those with extended service intervals can still experience tensioner fatigue.
items.repairVsReplace: A preventative tensioner and chain replacement is a straightforward specialist procedure (£2,500-£4,500). If ignored to the point of chain skip, catastrophic valve damage will necessitate a full Aston Martin AJ133S engine replacement.

items.title: Coolant Crossover Pipe Leaks
items.whatHappens: The AJ133S features plastic coolant crossover pipes situated in the valley of the V8. Extreme heat cycling causes these components to become brittle and crack, leading to slow coolant loss. If unchecked, this can result in overheating and potential cylinder head warping.
items.repairVsReplace: Gasket and pipe renewal is a standard, albeit labour-intensive, specialist procedure. It does not typically require a full unit replacement unless severe overheating has already occurred.

items.title: Supercharger Coupler Wear
items.whatHappens: The rubber isolator coupler between the supercharger snout and the drive pulley can degrade over time. This manifests as a rhythmic ticking or rattling noise from the front of the engine, particularly at idle or during deceleration, and can eventually lead to a loss of boost or supercharger damage.
items.repairVsReplace: Replacing the coupler is a relatively inexpensive fix (£500-£1,000). However, if the coupler has completely failed and caused internal supercharger damage, a full supercharger rebuild or replacement is required.

failures.goodYearsLine: The AJ133S is widely regarded by specialists as a robust and thoroughly developed performance engine. Catastrophic failures are exceptionally rare, with most issues being routine, high-value maintenance items rather than inherent design flaws .

variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the Aston Martin AJ133S
variants.intro: Because the AJ133 V8 family spans multiple Jaguar, Land Rover, and Aston Martin applications with varying power outputs, confirming your exact code is essential before purchasing a replacement. The AJ133S is the specific 430hp variant exclusive to the Vantage S. Where to find it: The engine code is stamped directly on the engine block (typically on the right-hand side near the oil filter housing) and is recorded on the vehicle's V5C registration document and Aston Martin provenance paperwork. Commonly confused codes: Owners frequently mistake the AJ133S for the standard AJ133 (the 385hp/430hp variant found in the Jaguar XF/XK and standard Aston Martin V8 Vantage) or the AJ133HP (the 550hp+ variant found in the Rapide S and DBS). Why it matters: While they share the same fundamental 5.0L supercharged architecture, the Aston Martin AJ133S features bespoke ECU mapping, specific supercharger pulley ratios, and unique exhaust routing tailored to the Vantage S chassis. Attempting to swap in a standard Jaguar AJ133 or a higher-output AJ133HP without the corresponding Aston Martin loom, ECU, and intake components will result in severe compatibility errors, restricted performance, and persistent check engine lights.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement Aston Martin AJ133S - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: A used Aston Martin AJ133S is only advisable if it comes with a comprehensive, stamped Aston Martin service history proving the timing chain tensioners, coolant pipes, and supercharger coupler have been recently inspected or replaced. Given the high-performance nature of this engine, buying a used Aston Martin AJ133S for sale with unknown maintenance is a high-risk gamble. Browse vetted used Aston Martin AJ133S engines for sale

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: This is the most balanced and recommended choice for most owners. A proper reconditioning process for the Aston Martin AJ133S will replace the timing chain tensioners, renew all valley coolant gaskets and pipes, and inspect the supercharger coupler. This restores the full 430hp output while eliminating the known weak points. Compare reconditioned Aston Martin AJ133S options

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A full rebuild is justified for high-mileage examples where the block is still sound but internal wear (such as piston ring or bearing wear) is advanced. A professional rebuild of the Aston Martin AJ133S will include new bottom-end bearings, line-boring if necessary, and all-new sealing components, offering near-new longevity for the V8 platform. Explore rebuilt Aston Martin AJ133S specifications

items.question: How much does an Aston Martin AJ133S engine replacement cost?
items.answer: A reconditioned Aston Martin AJ133S engine starts from £5,500 for supply-only, with fully fitted replacements typically ranging from £7,180 to £11,160 depending on the specialist. Prices vary based on whether the timing chain tensioners and valley coolant pipes are included in the rebuild scope. Labour typically requires 14-18 hours at Aston Martin specialist rates. Rebuilt units command a significant premium but include refreshed supercharger couplers and comprehensive internal inspections.

items.question: What is the most common failure with the Aston Martin AJ133S?
items.answer: The most documented failure pattern is timing chain tensioner wear and coolant crossover pipe leaks, typically occurring between 60,000 and 100,000 miles. The extreme heat in the V-configuration accelerates the degradation of plastic coolant pipes in the engine valley. Early tensioner fatigue can lead to chain slack and cold-start rattling. If coolant loss is ignored, it can result in overheating and cylinder head warping, necessitating a full unit replacement.

items.question: Which models use the AJ133S engine?
items.answer: The Aston Martin AJ133S was exclusively fitted to the Vantage S from 2012 to 2017. It delivers 430hp and serves as the specific high-output variant for this chassis, distinguishing it from the standard 4.7L V8 Vantage. It was never used in the DB9, Rapide, or standard V8 Vantage models. Always verify your specific fitment using your registration number.

items.question: Should I buy a used or reconditioned Aston Martin AJ133S?
items.answer: A reconditioned Aston Martin AJ133S is strongly recommended over a used unit to prevent catastrophic secondary damage. Used units carry a high risk of hidden tensioner degradation or brittle valley coolant pipes. A proper reconditioning process replaces the timing chain tensioners, renews all valley coolant gaskets and pipes, and inspects the supercharger coupler. Reconditioned units come with a 12 to 24-month warranty, providing essential peace of mind for a high-value asset.

items.question: How do I know if my car has the AJ133S and not the standard AJ133?
items.answer: Check your V5C registration document or the physical stamp on the engine block. The AJ133S is the specific 430hp variant exclusive to the Vantage S. The standard AJ133 is the lower-output variant found in the standard V8 Vantage and Jaguar models. Fitting the wrong revision without the corresponding Aston Martin-specific loom, ECU, and intake components will result in severe compatibility errors and restricted performance.
